ctor.rationale: `base(3, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Rare, TargetType.RandomEnemy)` (BeatDown.cs:18-21) == cost 3 / SKILL / RARE / RANDOM_ENEMY. No keywords, no tags.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new CardsVar(3)` (BeatDown.cs:16) == `_cards = 3`, read as `DynamicVars.Cards.IntValue` at the Take site.

OnPlay.issue: The candidate FILTER is faithful (`c.Type == CardType.Attack && !c.Keywords.Contains(CardKeyword.Unplayable)` on the discard pile, BeatDown.cs:26, == `c.card_type == CardType.ATTACK and c.is_playable` over `ctx.player.discard_pile`), and so is the per-card auto-play with the loop's early exit. THE SELECTION IS NOT. C# does `.ToList().StableShuffle(Owner.RunState.Rng.Shuffle).Take(IntValue)`: StableShuffle first SORTS the list (`list2.Sort()`, ListExtensions.cs:22-31 -- by CardModel.CompareTo, i.e. the canonical UPPERCASE-id order noted in the seed facts) so the result no longer depends on discard-pile order, THEN Fisher-Yates shuffles it on the named **Shuffle** stream. The sim calls `ctx.combat._rng.shuffle(candidates)` (colorless_skills.py:113): the unseeded shared `random.Random`, not `ctx.combat.combat_rng.shuffle` (the accessor exists -- combat_rng.py:17,50), with NO pre-sort, and Python's `random.shuffle` is a different Fisher-Yates variant. Three independent divergences stack: wrong stream, missing stabilising sort (so identical discard contents in a different order pick different cards), and a different draw sequence. Observable: under a string-seeded parity run Beat Down auto-plays a different set of attacks than the recorded run and desyncs the Shuffle stream for every later reshuffle. LIVE -- Beat Down is a ported Rare colorless Skill and the Shuffle parity stream is already wired (`CombatRng.parity`, combat_rng.py:41-46). REGRESSION TEST: `test/test_rng_tripwire.py:33` (`test_no_wrong_stream_draws_in_random_run`, 20 seeded full runs) is the standing gate for this whole family. It wraps `RunState.rng` and asserts ZERO in-combat draws on it; `CombatState` receives that same object as `self._rng` (run.py:1146-1148, combat.py:88), so a `ctx.combat._rng` draw taken from inside a card's `on_play` is recorded and fails the gate -- verified by playing this family's shape under a `Tripwire` and getting a hit at the `card.on_play` frame (combat.py:490). The gate is green today, so these 20 seeds never reach this card's draw; routing the site to the named `combat_rng` accessor is verified by keeping it green.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars.Cards.UpgradeValueBy(1m)` (BeatDown.cs:49) == `self._cards += 1` (3 -> 4). Downgrade-safe; `card_probes.py downgrade` does not list beat_down.

guards.rationale: == `if ctx.combat.is_over or ctx.player.is_dead: break` (colorless_skills.py:115-116). Both stop auto-playing the remaining attacks once the combat has been decided mid-loop.

guards.what: target selection for AnyEnemy attacks: C# rolls `Rng.CombatTargets.NextItem(CombatState.HittableEnemies)` in BeatDown itself and passes it to AutoPlay; the sim lets `auto_play_card` roll (BeatDown.cs:32-40)
guards.issue: The stream is right on both sides -- `combat.auto_play_card` uses `self.combat_rng.targets.choice(living)` with the CardCmd.cs:77 citation in-line (combat.py:540-546) -- and the candidate set matches (`living` = not `is_gone` == HittableEnemies). What differs is WHEN the draw is taken. C# rolls the target BEFORE calling `CardCmd.AutoPlay`, so the CombatTargets draw is spent even if AutoPlay then declines to play the card; the sim rolls it INSIDE `auto_play_card`, after the `card.is_playable` and `hooks.should_play_card(card, auto_play=True)` checks (combat.py:536-546), so a hook-blocked play spends no draw. Under seed parity a differing draw COUNT is an observable desync. DORMANT: BeatDown's own filter already excludes Unplayable cards, so only a `should_play_card` preventer can reach the divergence, and no such preventer is ported that fires on an auto-played Attack -- it goes live the moment one is (any C# `ShouldPlayCard` implementer for Attack cards).

guards.what: cards are taken from the DISCARD pile and auto-played from there; the played card ends in its normal result pile
guards.rationale: `auto_play_card` removes the card from whichever of hand/draw/discard/exhaust holds it before resolving (combat.py:526-535) and routes it through `_resolve_card_play`, matching CardCmd.AutoPlay's pile handling. Beat Down itself is in the discard-pile limbo while this runs (combat.py:452-454) but is a Skill, so it is never its own candidate.
